Session 2 = knowledge gradient and one-step lookahead, high-dimensional BO, self-driving labs, the A-Lab critique, companies, LLMs in the loop (Parts 3-6). Extra application examples follow Further reading. Caption is verbatim from arXiv v3, p. 3; the cut final sentence is "Figure 3 shows a sample meta-prompt for prompt optimization." Every step evaluates all 8 generated solutions; the meta-prompt keeps only the top 20 by score (p. 8), which is the "selection" in the roles table. No uncertainty model: the LLM reads sorted scores, rounded to integers. The paper's ablation (Fig. 7c-d, p. 16) found that hiding the scores made optimization worse.

GSM8K: PaLM 2-L scorer, 1,319 test problems (Table 1, p. 1). "Let's think step by step" is Kojima et al. 2022, hand-written. Table 1 and Table 4 pick "the instruction with the highest test accuracy" per optimizer, so 80.2% is the best of several on test, not a single pre-registered pick. Training subset: 3.5% of GSM8K's 7,473 training problems; 20% of each BBH task, the other 80% is the test set (pp. 9, 11). BBH counts are Table 7 (p. 32) test column, PaLM 2-L scorer. The paper's own "over 5% on 19/23 tasks" (p. 11) is on training+test accuracy. Panel (b), movie_recommendation, text-bison scorer: 90.0% test vs 63.0% for "Let's think step by step" (Table 7). The one loss: tracking_shuffled_objects_seven_objects, 16.5% vs 61.5%. TSP: 5 random instances per size, gap vs Gurobi optimum; the heuristic is farthest insertion, which beats every LLM from 20 points up (Table 3, p. 6). At 50 points the other optimizers are far worse: text-bison 219.8%, gpt-3.5-turbo 133.0% ("up to 20x worse optimality gaps", p. 6).

All methods used Mistral-large-2407; the logo in the diagram is generic. Theory: regret = support + discovery + selection error; the selection term scales with the GP information gain over the generator-reachable set, not the full domain.
